regions.text: 宗教家達にとつては啓示は必ずしも好む道嗜む業ではなかつた。

quote.translation: For the great religious figures revelation was not necessarily a path they liked or a work they relished.

regions.text: ...啓示は彼等にとつては無限の光茶と歓喜とを宿す運命—兎に角測命であつた』改多野特一、东教哲摩三二ー三三真）。

quote.translation: For them revelation was fate, holding infinite glory and joy, at any rate fate" (Hatano Seiichi, Philosophy of Religion, pp. 32-33).

regions.text: 運命こは目々偶然が一方に因果必然と結合し他方に目約々必然と結合して無限大へ擴大されると共に無限小へ縮小されたものであると云つた。

quote.translation: I said that fate is teleological contingency which, combining on the one hand with causal necessity and on the other with teleological necessity, has been expanded to the infinitely large and at the same time contracted to the infinitely small.

regions.text: きうしてその場合強ひて分析をなすならば目前々偶然と因果前必然との結合は「盲日的運命」として現はれ、目々偶然と目々必然との結合は「攝理」をして現はれる。

quote.translation: If we force an analysis, the combination of teleological contingency with causal necessity appears as "blind fate", and the combination of teleological contingency with teleological necessity as "providence".

regions.text: ヘーゲルによれば古代人のHEapcopiworfsipappienは盲日運命であり、キスト教は合目的性の導入によつて神の攝理を說くるのである。前者は「包彼を脱がない必然性』（wenthilteNotwendigkcit）であり、後者は『包被を脱いだ必然性』（enthilteNotwendigkeit）である。前者は育日的で慰めなき立場であり後者は先見で慰めの立場であ6（Fegel,Encyklopidie,hrsg.v.Bolland，§147,Zustz,S197-2m）。

quote.translation: According to Hegel, the πεπρωμένον and εἱμαρμένη of the ancients are blind fate, whilst Christianity, by introducing purposiveness, teaches the providence of God; the former is "necessity that has not cast off its veil" (unenthüllte Notwendigkeit), the latter "necessity that has cast off its veil" (enthüllte Notwendigkeit), and the former is a blind and comfortless standpoint, the latter a foreseeing and consoling one (Hegel, Encyklopädie, hrsg. v. Bolland, § 147, Zusatz, S. 197-200).

regions.text: しかしながら運命概念の特色は寧ろ斯やうに二種の運命に散然だる區別を許さぬ點にあると思ふ。既に云つたやうに意識を無意歌をの間には段階約御進前通

quote.translation: Yet the distinctive feature of the concept of fate lies, I think, rather in its not permitting so sharp a distinction between two kinds of fate, since, as I have already said, between consciousness and the unconscious there is a graded and gradual passage.
